title: Two distinct paths for image generation
summary:
New image-generation paths, a Qwen3 Coder switch, and more capable Gemini tools made this a model-heavy day.

A two-step SANA-Sprint 1.6B image-generation backend was added. Flux Schnell also returned as its own model: requests for `flux` no longer resolve to `zimage`, which remains the default.

The `qwen-coder` API name now routes to Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, with new Qwen3 aliases and an 8,192-token limit. Enter’s model pricing table now shows full model names and groups text, image, and video models in one place.

Gemini requests gained support for `code_execution`, `google_search`, and caller-supplied `url_context`. Chat responses now accept generated image blocks, including plots from code execution. `gemini-fast` no longer adds code execution by default, avoiding conflicts with structured-output requests.

highlights.title: SANA-Sprint image backend
highlights.text: SANA-Sprint 1.6B gained a two-step image-generation backend, adding another path for creating images.

highlights.title: Flux is Flux again
highlights.text: Choose `flux` for Flux Schnell rather than being routed to `zimage`. `zimage` remains the default. [Browse Flux](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=flux).

highlights.title: Qwen Coder moves to Qwen3
highlights.text: Use `qwen-coder` to reach Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, with an 8,192-token limit. [Browse the model](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=qwen-coder).

highlights.title: More Gemini tools
highlights.text: Use `code_execution` with `gemini` and `gemini-large`, Google Search through `gemini-search`, or pass `url_context` in your tools array. [Explore the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).
